newsitem.title: USA: Connie Lee Insurance says has potential buyer.
newsitem.headline: Connie Lee Insurance says has potential buyer.

text.p: Connie Lee Insurance Co said it has received "expressions of interest" regarding the potential sale of the municipal bond insurance company, and it is exploring the idea.
Connie Lee, also known as the Construction Loan Insurance Corp, said in a statement it is reviewing "a range of strategic options, including the potential sale of the company."

"Connie Lee is responding to certain unsolicited expressions of interest it has received regarding a potential acquisition of the company," Oliver Sockwell, Connie Lee's President and Chief Executive Officer, said in the statement. "There can be no assurance that a sale or similar transaction will be consummated."
The Washington, D.C.-based company said it would make no other statements on the matter until the evaluation process is over.

Connie Lee was created by Congress in 1987 to insure bonds from colleges and universities whose credit characteristics did not meet the requirements of private bond insurers. The company completed a privatization earlier this year, enabling it to insure debt in all sectors of the municipal market.
Sockwell announced in April he would resign from the company in July.
